headline: A federal grand jury has indicted Andrew Kozak, an employee of BioUrja Renewables in Peoria, Illinois, in connection with Friday’s bomb threat at the ethanol facility, where authorities found and rendered safe a destructive device. Kozak was arrested at the facility as he reported for work yesterday morning. The indictment accuses him of sending an email to BioUrja indicating that explosive devices had been placed at the facility. He is charged with one felony count of threats regarding explosives and one felony count of interstate communication of a threat. The incident closed roads and forced everyone within 1 mile of the plant to evacuate until the all clear was given around 1 p.m. Saturday, an 18 hour order that displaced thousands of residents and shut down downtown businesses and events, including a concert by country music performer Jon Pardi. The indictment does not allege that Kozak placed the device discovered at the facility, however it is not uncommon for federal prosecutors to seek a superseding indictment, if warranted, after evidence has been forensically examined.

headline: Federal prosecutors in New York have charged Irish national Daithi O’Corrain with destruction of government property over an April 11th, 2026 attack on a U.S. Air National Guard C-130H at Shannon Airport in Ireland. The Justice Department says he breached the airport perimeter, broke into the parked aircraft, damaged its interior and cockpit instruments and its wiring and hydraulic lines. Prosecutors say the aircraft, worth about $60 million, was effectively destroyed and will not return to flight. Irish authorities arrested him April 11th and charged him two days later with criminal damage to the aircraft and to the airport perimeter fence, and with trespass. Irish media reported he later secured bail. The Justice Department’s release does not say whether O’Corrain is in custody or whether the U.S. will seek his extradition. The U.S. indictment cites earlier incidents at Shannon, including a van driven through the perimeter fence in May 2025, paint sprayed on a military aircraft that month, and a breach near a C-40 in November 2025.

headline: Greece's EYP and North Macedonia's ANB have foiled an alleged Iranian plot to carry out a terror attack or assassination in Greece. The target was an Israeli executive in Greece, according to sources. The executive was not named. Five North Macedonian nationals were arrested. Weapons, maps and notes were seized. The joint operation has been running since early 2026. The ANB named Iranian national Edris Jahangiri Mavaneh as the man directing the network. He is linked to Iranian security services and to drug lord Naji Sharifi Zindashti, per the ANB. The network held secret meetings in third countries, including Iran. It relied on local criminal ties for logistics.
